wiki-iran.standing: Daily readers of Wikipedia's article on Iran, the Islamic Republic on the Gulf whose southern coast lines the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow passage much of the world's seaborne oil must pass through.
wiki-iran.recent: Trump told the UN he could "annihilate" Iran on the same day Iranian officials held three hours of direct talks with Witkoff and offered to reopen Hormuz. Through Qatar, Tehran then set its terms: end the naval blockade and release frozen assets. Days later, all 4 Iraqi airports halted Iran flights under new US sanctions.

brent.standing: The price of a barrel of light North Sea crude, and the benchmark most internationally traded oil is priced against. Refiners, airlines and importing governments pay after it, and petrol and diesel prices follow it.
brent.recent: Hormuz is shut by the Iran war, and Iran says it reopens 7 days after the US accepts its ceasefire offer. France sent soldiers and radars to guard Yanbu, the Saudi hub for oil that avoids the strait. Congress also passed a Russia sanctions bill letting Trump tariff Russian-oil buyers up to 100%.

wti.standing: West Texas Intermediate: US light, low-sulphur crude delivered at Cushing, Oklahoma, and the benchmark US oil futures settle on. It sets what American refiners pay, and petrol and diesel prices follow it.
wti.recent: With Hormuz shut, Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline to Yanbu was the Gulf's only bypass. Mid-September attacks shut it, and crude peaked. Its restart pulled prices back. Meanwhile drone strikes on Russian refineries helped push US diesel to a record, and the White House drew up a 90-day diesel export ban.

natgas-hh.standing: The US benchmark price for natural gas, set at a pipeline hub in Louisiana where interstate lines meet. It prices American power generation and home heating, and the feedgas behind US LNG exports.
natgas-hh.recent: The fortnight's gas news was elsewhere: Saudi Arabia's only Hormuz bypass shut, and China and India switched to coal and oil when gas cargoes did not arrive. Neither is a US supply or demand event, and none of it accounts for the Henry Hub price.

wheat.standing: The IMF's monthly world price for a tonne of wheat, drawn from US export quotations. Wheat supplies about a fifth of the calories people eat, and big importers such as Egypt budget their bread subsidies against it.
wheat.recent: The fortnight's wheat reporting was agronomy rather than markets: research datelined Cairo found that early heat costs wheat the most grain. US diesel hit a record $6.31 a gallon, raising the cost of growing and moving food, but that came after the latest monthly price and does not account for its rise.

rice.standing: Thai white rice with 5% broken grains, priced for export from Bangkok, and the benchmark for the world's rice trade. Importers from Manila to Dakar buy against it, and India's export rules move it more than any harvest.
rice.recent: This fortnight's rice news was about the plant, not its price: El Niño disrupted planting and water supply in Agusan del Sur, a Hyderabad field trial found a growth regulator strengthened rice stalks, and London researchers traced how blast fungus breaks down the plant's defences. None of it explains the fall in the export price.

copper.standing: The IMF's benchmark price for a tonne of refined copper, the metal in nearly every wire, motor and grid line. Chile and Peru mine the most of it and China uses about half, so it works as a gauge of industrial demand.

us-10y.standing: The yield on ten-year US government debt, the rate that mortgages, corporate loans and emerging-market borrowing are priced against. It rises when investors expect more inflation, tighter Fed policy or heavier federal borrowing.
us-10y.recent: The Fed raised rates 12-0, tightening into a supply shock caused by a closed strait, and the 10-year crossed 5% for the first time in 19 years in the days around the vote. Treasury volatility then jumped from 80 to 104 in two days while stocks stayed calm, and average global government yields reached their highest since 2007.

sp500.standing: About 500 large US companies, picked by a committee at S&P Dow Jones Indices and weighted by market value. It is the main gauge of American stocks, a few tech giants make up much of it, and pension and index funds around the world track it.
sp500.recent: A warning from inside the AI industry started a global sell-off in mid-September, with chip stocks down 8%. When the Fed raised rates days later, the market stayed calm. Meanwhile the MOVE index of Treasury volatility climbed while the VIX stayed flat: bond traders are pricing in oil costs from the war and strained government finances, and stock investors are not.

nasdaq100.standing: The 100 largest non-financial companies listed on the Nasdaq Stock Market in the US, weighted by market value. A handful of tech giants dominate it, so it works as the market's running price on big tech and AI.
nasdaq100.recent: Chip stocks led a global sell-off on Sep 14 as fears of an AI apocalypse went mainstream, which hit an index built on those same companies. A day earlier Anthropic picked Nasdaq for an IPO that could reportedly raise $100 billion at $2 trillion. Nothing reported explains the rebound that followed.

us-gas-retail.standing: The average price of a gallon of regular gasoline at US pumps, as surveyed by the EIA. It passes crude and refining costs straight through to drivers, and it is the fuel price American households feel most directly.
us-gas-retail.recent: Refined fuel tightened, not just crude: the Iran war's Hormuz shock put Brent near $107, and Ukrainian drones halted the Moscow refinery supplying 40% of city fuel. As US diesel hit a record $6.51, Trump pressed Kyiv to stop hitting Russian refineries and the White House prepared a 90-day diesel exports ban.

natgas-ttf.standing: The wholesale gas price at the Title Transfer Facility, the Dutch trading hub that sets Europe's benchmark. Power bills and industrial costs across the continent follow it, and it competes with Asia for the same LNG cargoes.
natgas-ttf.recent: Europe is bidding against Asia for scarce LNG to fill its storage. In mid-September, October futures in Amsterdam reached $1,004 per 1,000 cubic meters, the first time above $1,000 since Dec 2022. China and India stepped back and burned coal and oil instead of gas, with their LNG demand expected to return when the Mideast war ends.

vix.standing: The CBOE Volatility Index: the 30-day swing that options traders price into the S&P 500, the broad index of large US companies. It rises when investors pay up to insure against a fall, which is why it is called Wall Street's fear gauge.
vix.recent: The fortnight's one volatility story came from bonds, not stocks: in New York, Treasury volatility jumped from 80 to 104 in 2 days. Neither that nor the escalating Saudi oil crisis and the Red Sea tension in the headlines explains the calm in equity options.

fx-pkr.standing: How many Pakistani rupees one US dollar buys. Pakistan imports most of its fuel and has leaned on repeated IMF programmes, so this rate carries oil prices and lender conditions into prices at home.
fx-pkr.recent: Pakistan held its policy rate with Brent near $110 a barrel, Saudi crude to its refineries stopped as the Bab al-Mandab chokepoint came under threat, and the IMF asked for 174 legislative amendments ahead of the fourth review of its $7bn programme. None of these moved the rupee much.

fx-ngn.standing: How many naira buy one US dollar, so a rising line means a weaker naira. Oil earns most of Nigeria's dollars and imports spend them, so the rate passes quickly into the prices Nigerians pay.
fx-ngn.recent: Two things changed how many dollars Nigeria needs and how many flow in. Dangote ran at 105% capacity and petrol imports fell 26%, which cut a fuel bill paid in dollars. Nigeria's return to a bond index was expected to draw $17.5 billion. August inflation also fell to 15.39%.

fx-egp.standing: How many Egyptian pounds buy one US dollar, so a higher number means a weaker pound. Egypt imports much of its wheat and fuel and earns dollars from Suez Canal tolls, tourism and remittances, so the rate feeds straight into bread and energy costs.
fx-egp.recent: The fortnight carried Egypt's hunt for hard currency and debt relief: Maspero handed over 44 assets worth LE18.06 billion to settle debt, and the army-linked Future of Egypt moved into medical tourism to earn tourist dollars. Neither accounts for the pound's move.

fx-try.standing: The number of Turkish lira one US dollar buys. Turkey imports most of its energy and has lived with high inflation for years, so a weaker lira passes quickly into domestic prices, and the central bank manages how fast it falls.
fx-try.recent: Turkey's news this fortnight was mostly about security and diplomacy: an offer to meet Saudi Arabia's military needs, a base at Bashiqa passing to Iraqi control, and Erdogan's call to abolish the UN Security Council veto. The one economic item, Ankara's cut to its medium-term growth forecast, does not on its own explain the lira's drift.

fx-bdt.standing: Bangladesh's currency, quoted here as taka per US dollar and managed by the central bank. It depends on dollars earned by garment exports and sent home by workers abroad, and fuel and food imports use them up.
fx-bdt.recent: Bangladesh's news this fortnight was about borders and diplomacy: India pushed residents across at Chapainawabganj, 17,031 migrants were lured to Cambodia with promised jobs, and Tarique Rahman prepared for a US visit. None of it accounts for the rate.

fx-idr.standing: How many rupiah one US dollar buys, so a rising line means a weaker rupiah. The currency of Southeast Asia's largest economy moves with its coal, palm oil and nickel exports, and with how much foreign investors want its government bonds.
fx-idr.recent: The rupiah weakened after Prabowo fired finance minister Purbaya, who learned of it by phone mid-meeting, and gave the post to Suahasil. Three days later, lawmakers in Jakarta were debating breaking Indonesia's 3% deficit ceiling. Holders of the currency read that legal cap as the test of the government's fiscal discipline.

fx-lbp.standing: The Lebanese pound's dollar rate, which lost over 95% of its value after the 2019 banking collapse. The central bank has held it near one level since 2023, so it tracks policy in Beirut rather than daily news.
fx-lbp.recent: The fortnight's news from Lebanon was Israeli shelling of Zawtar al-Sharqiyah in the Nabatieh district and attacks on towns around Tyre, and none of it reached the rate.

fx-cny.standing: The price of one US dollar in onshore Chinese yuan. The People's Bank of China sets a fixing every day and lets the rate trade only within a band around it, and that level sets what Chinese exports cost abroad.
fx-cny.recent: Xi's three-day Washington visit brought trade pledges and a request that Trump stop saying he does not support Taiwan independence and say he opposes it instead. The South China Morning Post found the visit wrapped with little changed, and nothing from it accounts for the rate.

fx-inr.standing: How many Indian rupees one US dollar buys, so a rising line means a weaker rupee. India pays for most of its imported oil in dollars, so this rate carries crude prices into fuel and food costs across the country.
fx-inr.recent: Congress passed a sweeping sanctions bill targeting Russia that lets Trump tariff Russian-oil buyers up to 100%, a direct threat to India's energy supply. With Brent near $102.5, the oil import bill rose anyway, and foreign investors built record index-futures shorts of 290,041 contracts against Indian stocks.

fx-brl.standing: How many Brazilian reais one US dollar buys. The currency moves with Brazil's exports of soybeans, iron ore and oil, and with interest rates high enough to draw carry traders, who leave quickly when worries about public finances rise.
fx-brl.recent: The fortnight's news from Brazil was political. Lula raised Bolsa Família payments 15% by decree, polls showed Flávio Bolsonaro tied with him, and the Banco Master scandal spread through Brazilian politics. None of it accounts for where the real traded.

fx-mxn.standing: How many Mexican pesos one US dollar buys, so a rise means a weaker peso. It is one of the most traded emerging-market currencies, and it carries Mexico's exposure to US trade policy and remittances.
fx-mxn.recent: The weakest stretch came as Polo jumped from tropical storm to Category 5 off Manzanillo and then lashed Mexico. In the same days, 14 Latin American nations declared cartels foreign terrorist organizations, and Trump used his UN speech to flex U.S. dominance over the Western Hemisphere. None of the reporting ties the currency directly to either.

fx-eur.standing: How many euros one US dollar buys, on the most traded currency pair in the world. It sets what euro-area importers pay for oil and other goods priced in dollars, and how much European exporters' dollar earnings are worth at home.
fx-eur.recent: The fortnight's European news was about fuel. French diesel averaged a record 2.41 euros a litre, Eni capped pump prices in Italy, and France sent soldiers and radars to guard Yanbu, a Saudi oil hub. None of it reports a central-bank decision or data release that explains the exchange rate.

fx-jpy.standing: How many yen one US dollar buys. A weaker yen lifts Japanese exporters' profits and raises the cost of the fuel and food Japan imports, and the gap between Japanese and US interest rates drives much of its path.
fx-jpy.recent: The Bank of Japan lifted its rate to 1.25%, a 31-year high, to curb rising prices, but the US Fed had raised two days earlier, so the yield gap that pulls money out of yen narrowed less than a lone hike implies. The BOJ Governor's 75-minute briefing failed to win over markets. The yen's early-September rise came before both.

fx-rub.standing: How many rubles one US dollar buys. Russia's oil and gas export earnings largely set the rate, along with the Bank of Russia's interest rates and the capital controls in place since 2022, which limit how freely it trades.
fx-rub.recent: The fortnight's pressure on Moscow pointed the other way: Congress passed a sanctions bill that lets Trump tariff Russian-oil buyers up to 100%, and Trump pressed Ukraine to stop hitting Russian fuel plants. Neither accounts for the ruble firming against the dollar.

fx-zar.standing: How many South African rand one US dollar buys, so a higher reading means a weaker rand. It is among the most traded emerging-market currencies, and it moves with platinum and gold prices and with foreign appetite for local bonds.
fx-zar.recent: The rand's weakest day came the day after Washington imposed visa curbs on South Africa, the latest round of US sanctions. Pretoria disputes them and says it has met 2 of 5 US demands. The measures rest on a claim of white persecution, and 12,901 of 12,904 US refugee admissions went to South Africans.

btc.standing: The largest cryptocurrency: a fixed-supply digital token recorded on a public ledger with no central issuer. It trades around the clock and moves on US interest rates, crypto regulation and corporate treasury buying.
btc.recent: The slide came when the US Senate's crypto bill collapsed, knocking 5% off bitcoin as corporate buying fell to 5,900 coins. The rebound came when $647.9 million of short bets were liquidated. Gains faded after traders priced in 4 Fed rate hikes by June 2027 and hackers took $352 million from Bitget.

eth.standing: The native currency of the Ethereum blockchain, paid as fees to run smart contracts and staked to secure the network. Much of decentralised finance settles on it, so its price follows demand for that activity.
eth.recent: The one direct signal was fund buying: Ethereum ETFs took in $216 million on Friday while Bitcoin's lost money for a fourth day. The Senate crypto bill then collapsed and Bitcoin fell 5%. Hot-wallet thefts followed, with 2,234 ether taken from Duelbits and $352 million from Bitget, and none of this accounts for the price.

paxg.standing: A Paxos-issued token, each backed by one troy ounce of gold held in London vaults, so it trades at the spot gold price. Gold pays no yield, so it tends to fall when interest rates are expected to rise.
paxg.recent: Higher oil prices stoked bets on a September Fed rate hike, and gold, which pays no interest, sold off alongside silver and tech stocks. The fortnight's other gold news, Hong Kong's push to become an international trading hub and the Financial Conduct Authority weighing rules for tokenized gold, was structural and did not move the price.

wiki-artificial-intelligence.standing: A daily count of reads of Wikipedia's article on artificial intelligence, the field of building software that learns, reasons and handles language. It rises with model launches and with political fights over who should regulate them.
wiki-artificial-intelligence.recent: AI chiefs asked the Security Council in New York for rules, but the US and China refused to sign the pact 20 nations sought, and Trump called global AI oversight a globalist scheme. China also rejected Dario Amodei's call to slow AI, in the same days Anthropic cut Opus prices 40% with its 5.5 release.

wiki-russia.standing: Daily reads of Wikipedia's article on Russia, the world's largest country by area. As a nuclear power, a major oil and gas exporter and a party to the war in Ukraine, it is a place people look up when events there reach their own lives.
wiki-russia.recent: United Russia took nearly 58% of the vote in a wartime Duma election, a day after Ukraine drones hit Moscow and killed a 44-year-old woman and an elderly man. Days later Trump pressed Kyiv to stop hitting Russian fuel plants, and Rubio invited ICC-wanted Vladimir Putin to the G20 in Miami.

wiki-china.standing: Daily reads of Wikipedia's article on China, the country as a whole. It rises when Beijing itself becomes the story, such as a summit, a trade dispute or a military shake-up, rather than a single company or city.
wiki-china.recent: Xi Jinping's three-day visit to Washington ended with little changed. Before he arrived, the US and China failed to extend their trade truce, and during the visit a US envoy said Beijing had assured Washington it isn't aiding Iran. Days earlier a purge of top generals left Xi's own military commission with just two members.

wiki-strait-of-hormuz.standing: How many people read Wikipedia's article on the Strait of Hormuz each day. The strait is the channel between Iran and Oman through which about a fifth of the world's seaborne oil, and most Gulf gas, leaves for Asia.
wiki-strait-of-hormuz.recent: Drones shut Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, the only route that skips Hormuz, while the Houthis moved on Bab el-Mandeb, so both Saudi export corridors were constrained at once and Brent went above $100. Only three vessels transited Hormuz on one Wednesday, and Iran has since sent its terms to Washington through mediators.

wiki-india.standing: Daily reads of the English Wikipedia article on India, the world's most populous country and a nuclear-armed democracy. It is the page readers land on when they want the basic facts behind a story from South Asia.
wiki-india.recent: Modi hosted a BRICS summit where Xi took centre stage and Iran sought easier access to the NDB. Meanwhile the US Congress passed a sanctions bill that lets Trump tariff Russian-oil buyers up to 100%. At home, Gandhi demanded the election chief quit over a voter purge, and a UPI fee on payments above Rs 2,000 was challenged in the Supreme Court.

cp:hormuz.standing: One-fifth of global seaborne oil passes through this 21-mile strait between Iran and Oman.
cp:hormuz.recent: The Iran war has all but closed the strait, and Tehran is using it as leverage: after three hours of direct talks with Witkoff, Iran offered that Hormuz opens 7 days after the US agrees. A Saudi pipeline restart that moves crude around the strait pushed Brent below $98, while US diesel hit a record $6.51 a gallon.

cp:bab-el-mandeb.standing: Between Yemen and Djibouti — the Red Sea’s southern gate. Houthi attacks since 2023 have pushed container shipping to reroute around Africa.
cp:bab-el-mandeb.recent: Houthis seized the Red Sea port of Mocha on 10 September, putting their advance on the coast beside the strait, and then declared a "blockade for blockade" against Saudi Arabia. They denied a report they had planted mines in Bab al-Mandeb. Italy sent warships without waiting for the EU, and Saudi crude to Pakistani refineries has stopped.

cp:suez.standing: Egypt’s 120-mile artery carries roughly 12% of global trade. The 2021 closure disrupted supply chains for weeks; Red Sea instability keeps it volatile.
cp:suez.recent: The canal's southern approach runs through Bab al-Mandeb, where the Houthis denied planting mines and, after a US official met them in Oman, said only Saudi-flagged vessels remain targets. With Hormuz shut, Saudi crude leaves from Yanbu up the Red Sea, and France is sending forces to defend those facilities.

cp:malacca.standing: Between Malaysia and Sumatra — the fastest route between the Indian and Pacific Oceans. Over 80,000 ships a year, including most of China’s oil imports.
cp:malacca.recent: The region's shipping news in September came from elsewhere: Iran's Strait Authority went after tanker insurers, Iran struck a tanker, and Hormuz vessel traffic fell to two. Closer by, haze from Sumatra peat fires eased over Singapore. None of it accounts for Malacca's traffic.

cp:taiwan.standing: Between mainland China and Taiwan — roughly 40% of the world’s container traffic passes through, and the flashpoint of any US–China confrontation.
cp:taiwan.recent: Xi used his Washington visit to press Trump to move US policy from not supporting Taiwan independence to opposing it, days after the US and China failed to extend their trade truce and Beijing purged its top generals. None of it has changed the ships moving through the strait.

cp:panama.standing: 50-mile shortcut between the Atlantic and Pacific. Drought in 2023–24 cut daily transits by half — a live example of climate binding to trade.

cp:bosporus.standing: Istanbul’s 20-mile waterway links the Black Sea to the Mediterranean — the only route for Russian naval access and Ukrainian grain exports.
cp:bosporus.recent: The fortnight's news from Ankara ran to an offer to meet Saudi Arabia's military needs and the handover of the Bashiqa base to Iraqi control. None of it touched Black Sea shipping, and none of it accounts for the lighter traffic through the strait.

cp:gibraltar.standing: 8 miles between Morocco and Spain — the only Atlantic–Mediterranean link. A surveillance chokepoint for Russian submarines and sanctioned oil.
cp:gibraltar.recent: The fortnight's news from either shore of the strait was about people rather than ships: riot police firing rubber bullets to clear migrants from Ceuta's beaches, and the palace party winning Morocco's election on its lowest turnout since 2007. None of it accounts for the traffic.

cp:dover.standing: The busiest shipping lane on Earth — 400+ ships a day squeeze through the English Channel’s 21-mile narrows.
cp:dover.recent: The fortnight's only Channel story was not about shipping: an anti-migrant activist slashed an empty migrant dinghy mid-Channel off Dover. France's new military commitment went to guarding Saudi oil at Yanbu, far from this lane, and nothing reported accounts for the merchant traffic here.

cp:cape-of-good-hope.standing: The 3,000-mile detour around southern Africa — the alternative when the Red Sea is closed. The new default for tankers since Houthi attacks began.
cp:cape-of-good-hope.recent: The fortnight's shipping shocks were in the Gulf: Iran struck a tanker, a tanker was attacked off Oman, and traffic through Hormuz fell to two vessels. Saudi crude to Pakistani refineries stopped. A blockage inside the Gulf strands cargo rather than sending it round Africa, so none of this accounts for traffic past the Cape.

cp:kerch.standing: Between Crimea and Russia — the only access to the Sea of Azov. A flashpoint since 2014 and contested throughout the Russia–Ukraine war.
cp:kerch.recent: The war news of the past fortnight was about Russian strikes on Kyiv and Kharkiv, and about Trump pressing Ukraine to stop hitting Russian fuel plants. None of it mentions the strait or explains why ships stopped using it.

mkt:tadawul.standing: The Tadawul All Share Index, which tracks every main-market company on the Saudi Exchange in Riyadh. It is the Arab world's largest market by value and Aramco dominates it. It trades Sunday to Thursday, so it opens the global week.
mkt:tadawul.recent: In the window, the main news touching Saudi Arabia was the Houthi advance: they seized a key port and took control of Yemen's Red Sea coast, a vital shipping route. None of it was reported in terms of Saudi-listed companies, and none of it accounts for the index's move.

mkt:bist.standing: The 100 largest companies on Borsa İstanbul, Türkiye's only stock exchange. It is priced in lira, so it carries the country's inflation as much as its earnings, and its direction says more than its level.
mkt:bist.recent: The slide came as Ankara cut its medium-term growth forecast, which wrote the regional war into the government's own numbers. In the same weeks Turkey offered to meet Saudi Arabia's military needs after drone attacks from Iraq, and agreed to hand the Bashiqa base to Iraqi control.

mkt:dfm.standing: The Dubai Financial Market General Index tracks the shares listed on Dubai's stock exchange, the Gulf's main listing venue for property and banking. It trades Monday to Friday, unlike Riyadh.
mkt:dfm.recent: The fortnight brought the war to Dubai's doorstep. Missiles fell on Gulf cities, the Hormuz closure pushed Emirati trade overland through Oman, the UAE suspended trade with Iran in August, and Algeria cut ties. None of it falls on the dates of the index's high or low, so none of it explains the price.

mkt:bursa-malaysia.standing: The Kuala Lumpur Composite Index tracks the 30 largest companies on Bursa Malaysia, the country's stock exchange. Bursa is also the world's largest market for Islamic finance instruments and the centre of the global sukuk trade.
mkt:bursa-malaysia.recent: Malaysia's September news was political and diplomatic: Najib paid $12.3 million for house arrest in the 1MDB case, Anwar Ibrahim held talks with Modi in New Delhi, and Mihas 2026 opened in Kuala Lumpur targeting $1.23 billion in halal trade. None of it accounts for the index's path.

mkt:idx.standing: The composite index of every company listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange in Jakarta, the benchmark for Southeast Asia's largest economy. It is heavily weighted to banks and to coal, nickel and palm-oil producers.
mkt:idx.recent: Prabowo ousted Purbaya as finance minister, who learned of his firing by phone mid-meeting and handed the post to Suahasil. Three days later lawmakers in Jakarta debated breaking Indonesia's 3% deficit ceiling, the rule that caps government borrowing and anchors this bank-heavy market.

mkt:tse.standing: The Nikkei 225: 225 large companies listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange, Japan's main market, weighted by share price rather than company size. Asia's largest exchange, and the first major market to price each trading day.
mkt:tse.recent: The Bank of Japan lifted its rate to 1.25%, a 31-year high, to curb rising prices, and the governor's 75-minute briefing failed to win over markets; dearer money lifts the yen against the exporters that fill the index. Days earlier SoftBank, a heavy weight in the index, slumped 13% as markets priced an AI slowdown.

mkt:hkex.standing: The Hang Seng Index follows the largest companies listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. It is where mainland Chinese companies meet foreign capital, which makes it the clearest daily read on how investors price China.
mkt:hkex.recent: The fortnight's China news turned on trade with Washington. The US and China failed to extend their trade truce, and Xi's visit to Washington wrapped with little changed. Neither of those explains the summer's climb.

mkt:sse.standing: The SSE Composite covers every stock listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange, mainland China's main board. Foreign investors are largely kept out, so it follows Beijing's domestic policy more than global risk appetite.
mkt:sse.recent: The US and China failed to extend their trade truce, and Xi's visit to Washington wrapped with little changed. Separately, 110 listed solar firms were found to have cut 222,800 jobs in 2 years as overcapacity bit. None of this reporting is tied to the index's slide, and none of it accounts for the price.

mkt:krx.standing: The Korea Composite Stock Price Index, which covers every common stock on the main board of the Korea Exchange in Seoul. Samsung and SK Hynix dominate it, so it moves with the global memory-chip cycle.
mkt:krx.recent: The index's two heavyweights were both in the news over the fortnight. Samsung is doubling its memory output, and SK Hynix wants Intel to make its chips in Ohio. North Korea also fired missiles twice, the second time from Wonsan. None of this explains the index's fall, which came before all of it.

mkt:bse.standing: The Sensex tracks 30 of the largest companies on the Bombay Stock Exchange in Mumbai, and is the benchmark for Indian shares. The exchange was founded in 1875 and is the oldest in Asia.
mkt:bse.recent: Brent holding near $102.5 as the Iran war deepened fed straight into India's import bill, and Mumbai's shares fell with it. A second pressure landed on the same bill: a US sanctions law now lets Trump tariff buyers of Russian oil up to 100%, and India is one of those buyers.

mkt:sgx.standing: The Straits Times Index tracks the 30 largest companies on the Singapore Exchange. Banks and regional property dominate it, which makes it the main gauge of Southeast Asia's financial hub.
mkt:sgx.recent: The fortnight in Singapore brought Brent's slide on diplomacy hopes, easing haze and Circle's $400 million purchase of a payments licence network. None of it accounts for the index's move.

mkt:twse.standing: The capitalisation-weighted index of every common stock listed on the Taiwan Stock Exchange in Taipei. TSMC alone is roughly a third of it, which makes it the most concentrated major market on the map.
mkt:twse.recent: The fortnight's Taiwan news was diplomatic, not corporate: during his Washington visit Xi pressed Trump to move from saying the US 'does not support' Taiwan independence to openly 'opposing' it. That came after the last close, and none of it accounts for the climb.

mkt:set.standing: A capitalisation-weighted index of every common stock listed on the Stock Exchange of Thailand in Bangkok, the country's main market. It moves with tourism flows and with regional energy prices.

mkt:pse.standing: The PSE Composite Index: 30 of the largest, most traded companies on the Philippine Stock Exchange in Manila. It is a small market driven by the domestic economy, and money sent home by Filipinos working abroad moves the index.
mkt:pse.recent: The fortnight's Philippine news was a ferry fire off Coron, a school shooting in Banga, Bangsamoro's first parliamentary election and an anti-graft court's arrest warrant for Romualdez over flood-control kickbacks. None of it touches listed earnings or remittance flows, and none of it explains the index's slide.

mkt:asx.standing: The 200 largest listed companies on the Australian Securities Exchange in Sydney. Miners and banks dominate it, and it is often the first major market to react to Chinese demand data.
mkt:asx.recent: The ASX slumped on rate fears mid-month, as the Reserve Bank warned about imported inflation and a fiscal path it has never modelled spending cuts against. Fuel sharpened the worry: Trump weighed a diesel export ban after US diesel hit a record $6.52 a gallon, a direct threat to an importer like Australia.

mkt:jse.standing: The FTSE/JSE All Share Index, which tracks most of the companies listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange in South Africa. Africa's largest exchange by far, and the continent's only one with a usable public daily series.
mkt:jse.recent: The fortnight's news from South Africa was dominated by Washington: Rubio announced visa curbs on some South African nationals and promised more sanctions, and Pretoria said the US had misrepresented its policies. None of it was tied to listed companies, and nothing reported accounts for the index's path.

mkt:b3.standing: The Ibovespa is the benchmark of the most traded stocks on B3, Brazil's stock exchange in São Paulo. Iron ore, oil and Brazilian interest rates drive it, and it is Latin America's largest market.
mkt:b3.recent: The news out of Brazil was mostly about the election. Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro are tied at 47.7% and 47.4%, Brasília raised Bolsa Família payments 15% by decree before the vote, and the Banco Master scandal spread through Brazil politics. None of it explains the index's rise or its dips.

mkt:bmv.standing: The S&P/BMV IPC tracks about 35 of the most traded companies on the Mexican Stock Exchange in Mexico City. It is Mexico's benchmark, and it is tightly tied to US demand and to the peso.
mkt:bmv.recent: The fortnight's Mexican news was Hurricane Polo growing to Category 4 off Manzanillo and a Chinese backdoor hitting Latin American governments. Neither touches the companies in this index, and nothing reported explains its price.

mkt:byma.standing: The MERVAL tracks the most traded shares on Bolsas y Mercados Argentinos in Buenos Aires. Priced in a peso that keeps losing value, it rises even in bad years, so a day's direction means something and the level does not.
mkt:byma.recent: The fortnight's news out of Buenos Aires was political. INDEC data put poverty at 32.3% in the first half, its first rise since Milei's austerity began, landing as a test ahead of the election, while Milei pressed the Falklands claim at the UN. None of it is tied to the index's path in the reporting.

mkt:tsx.standing: The S&P/TSX Composite tracks the largest companies on the Toronto Stock Exchange, Canada's main market. Energy producers, miners and banks dominate it, so it trades more like a commodity basket than a broad equity index.
mkt:tsx.recent: Canada's news this fortnight was diplomatic, not financial: the EU floated associate membership, which Ottawa's own Brussels envoy then played down, and Trump opened talks to buy potash from Belarus as part of a trade fight with Canada. Neither accounts for the index's path.

mkt:nyse.standing: The S&P 500 tracks 500 of the largest US companies listed on the New York Stock Exchange and Nasdaq, weighted by market value. Its close sets the tone that every other market opens against.
mkt:nyse.recent: In the past fortnight the Fed raised rates, tech stocks sold off as fears about AI went mainstream, and average global government bond yields neared 4%, the highest since 2007. Higher yields shrink what future earnings are worth today, and that hits the tech giants hardest, which carry the most weight in the index.

mkt:lse.standing: The 100 largest companies by market value on the London Stock Exchange, Britain's main market. Most of their revenue is earned abroad, so a falling pound tends to push the index up.
mkt:lse.recent: The fortnight's London business news carried average global government bond yields near 4%, the highest since 2007, and Airtel Money's plan for a London initial public offering. Neither accounts for the index's path.

mkt:xetra.standing: The 40 largest companies listed on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange, Germany's main market. Its carmakers, chemical groups and industrial firms make it Europe's clearest read on export demand.
mkt:xetra.recent: The fortnight's German news was about carmakers and politics. Volkswagen wrote down $11.5 billion, mostly on Porsche, then recalled 2.86 million cars over one corroded bolt. Merz's party fell to 5.5% in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania. None of this explains the index's path.

mkt:euronext-paris.standing: France's benchmark index: 40 of the largest companies listed on Euronext Paris. Luxury houses and energy majors dominate it, which leaves it unusually exposed to Chinese consumer demand.
mkt:euronext-paris.recent: With Hormuz shut, diesel in France averaged a record 2.41 euros a litre. The Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development raised its 2027 inflation forecast to 3.6%, and France sent soldiers and radars to guard Saudi Arabia's Yanbu oil hub. None of this accounts for the index's slide directly.

mkt:euronext-amsterdam.standing: The AEX, or Amsterdam Exchange index: the 25 most traded companies on Euronext Amsterdam, the Netherlands' main market and the world's oldest exchange. Chip-equipment maker ASML carries much of its weight.

mkt:bme.standing: The 35 most liquid companies on the Bolsa de Madrid, Spain's main stock exchange. Its large banks earn heavily in Latin America, so it tracks both economies.
mkt:bme.recent: The fortnight's Spanish news was a CIA warning that Russia could launch drones from container ships at southern Europe, an 87-year-old's eviction in Madrid's housing crisis, and migrants cleared from Ceuta's beaches. None of it explains the index's path.

mkt:borsa-italiana.standing: The FTSE MIB tracks the 40 most traded companies on Borsa Italiana in Milan, Italy's main stock market. Banks and utilities dominate it, so it reacts more than any other European index to the spread on Italian sovereign debt.
mkt:borsa-italiana.recent: Italian news this fortnight was about schools and defence rather than money: Meloni's 30% cap on foreign pupils and the niqab ban, and Rome sending warships toward Bab al-Mandeb without waiting for the EU. Eni capping its pump prices was the one story about a listed company here, and none of it explains the index's path.

mkt:six.standing: The Swiss Market Index: the 20 largest companies on the SIX Swiss Exchange in Zurich, Switzerland's main market. Nestlé, Roche and Novartis carry it, which makes it defensive when the world turns risk-off.
mkt:six.recent: The Kremlin took control of Nestlé's Russia business by decree rather than through a court, and Nestlé said it was weighing all options. That is a blow to the index's heaviest name. But it came after the index had already bottomed, so it does not explain the earlier slide.

mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.standing: The 30 most traded companies on Nasdaq Stockholm, Sweden's main stock market. It leans heavily on industrials and telecoms, which makes it an early read on European capital spending.
mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.recent: Sweden's election was the main news from Stockholm. With 95% counted, the opposition bloc led 176 seats to 173, neither bloc could govern alone, and the Social Democrats got the first chance to form a new government. None of it explains the index's move.

mkt:tase.standing: The 125 largest companies by market value on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange, Israel's only public market. Banks, defence contractors and technology firms carry most of its weight, and it trades Sunday to Thursday.

wiki-donald-trump.standing: Daily readers of the English Wikipedia article on Donald Trump, the 45th and 47th president of the United States. Because his decisions reach trade, alliances and markets worldwide, readers far outside America look him up.
wiki-donald-trump.recent: Xi Jinping's three-day US trip ended with the trade truce extended to January 10, Scott Bessent said, and a joint pledge to keep AI under human control. The same week Trump banned CNN, Politico and MS NOW from the White House before they regained access, and Moscow said his nuclear test order threatens the moratorium.

wiki-united-states.standing: Daily reads of the English Wikipedia article on the United States, one of the encyclopedia's most-visited country pages. Reads rise with American elections, wars and summits, and fall back when Washington leaves the front page.
wiki-united-states.recent: Xi Jinping arrived for a three-day US trip as Trump pressed Beijing over Iran, and a US envoy said Beijing had given assurances it isn't aiding Iran. The same week, a court cleared the SAVE citizenship database for checking voter rolls, and the Justice Department joined X's appeal against a €120 million EU fine.

fed-funds.standing: The overnight rate the Federal Reserve's committee sets for lending between US banks. It is the base price of dollar credit, so mortgages, corporate debt and borrowing costs in every economy that borrows in dollars move with it.
fed-funds.recent: The Fed voted 12-0 on September 16 to raise rates, defying Trump's calls to lower them, and the cause was a closed strait feeding oil into the price index: US consumer prices rose 0.4% in August. Goldman Sachs had abandoned its no-hike call days earlier, and the 10-year Treasury yield hit 5% before the vote.

ecb-rate.standing: The interest the European Central Bank pays banks on money they park with it overnight, and in practice the euro area's policy rate. Mortgage costs, savings returns and the euro's exchange rate all move off it.
ecb-rate.recent: What the European Central Bank did in Frankfurt this fortnight was unrelated to its rate: it moved to close stablecoins' yield loophole and to hold blockchain-based bonds on its own books. Elsewhere, the Fed raised rates 12-0 over a closed strait, and the Bank Of Japan took its rate to a 31-year high.

us-unemployment.standing: The share of Americans in the labour force who are out of work and actively looking, measured each month by the Bureau of Labor Statistics survey of households. The Federal Reserve steers interest rates partly by it.

xag.standing: Silver priced through Kinesis's KAG token, each unit backed by an ounce of physical bullion held in vaults. Silver is both a monetary metal and an industrial one: solar panels and electronics consume roughly half of each year's supply.
xag.recent: In mid-September silver fell on the same day as gold and tech stocks while bitcoin climbed, so the decline was shared with gold rather than specific to silver. China's solar industry, a major user of the metal, was cutting jobs because it had built too much capacity, but no report here connects that to the price.

us-cpi.standing: How much prices paid by US urban consumers rose over the past year, measured by the Bureau of Labor Statistics. It shapes Federal Reserve rate decisions, Social Security adjustments and inflation-linked Treasury payouts.

portwatch-hormuz-tanker.standing: The daily count of tankers passing through the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow channel between Iran and Oman that is the only sea exit for most Gulf crude and gas. About a fifth of the world's oil normally moves through it.
portwatch-hormuz-tanker.recent: The strait has emptied as the Iran war moved onto the water. Two ships were attacked in the Strait of Hormuz, and drones shut Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, the only route that skips Hormuz. Iran has since held direct talks with Witkoff and offered to reopen the strait 7 days after the US agrees to its terms.

portwatch-bab-container.standing: The number of container ships a day passing through the strait between Yemen and Djibouti that links the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden. It is the southern gate of the Suez route, so Asia–Europe box freight depends on it staying open.
portwatch-bab-container.recent: The Houthis seized Mocha, the Red Sea port on the strait's Yemeni coast, on 10 September, then declared a "blockade for blockade" against Saudi Arabia. They say only Saudi-flagged vessels remain targets and deny a report that they planted mines in Bab al-Mandeb. Italy is sending warships of its own rather than waiting for the EU.

portwatch-suez-total.standing: The Suez Canal in Egypt links the Mediterranean to the Red Sea and is the shortest sea route between Europe and Asia. Ships reach it from the south through the Bab el-Mandeb strait, so trouble there empties the canal and cuts Egypt's toll income.
portwatch-suez-total.recent: Ships only reach the canal after clearing Bab al-Mandab at the Red Sea's southern mouth, and the Houthis fought for that coast: they seized the port of Mocha on 10 September, vowed "blockade for blockade" against Saudi Arabia and fired a missile at Riyadh. The G7 demanded Iran halt its arms support.

portwatch-panama-total.standing: The number of ships crossing the Panama Canal each day, the shortcut between the Atlantic and the Pacific. Its locks run on rain-fed lake water, so a drought cuts transits and delays US grain and gas bound for Asia.

portwatch-malacca-total.standing: The sea lane between the Malay Peninsula and Sumatra, the shortest route from the Indian Ocean to the Pacific. Most Gulf crude bound for China, Japan and South Korea passes through it, as does much Asia–Europe container trade.
portwatch-malacca-total.recent: The tanker news was at the far end of the route that feeds this strait. Saudi Arabia's only Hormuz bypass, the East-West pipeline, shut down, and Iran offered to reopen Hormuz after direct talks with Witkoff. None of the reports links either event to the number of ships passing through Malacca.

portwatch-taiwan-total.standing: Daily count of ships passing through the Taiwan Strait, the channel between Taiwan and mainland China that carries container traffic between Northeast Asia's ports and the rest of the world. Any military standoff there reroutes it.
portwatch-taiwan-total.recent: The fortnight's news on Taiwan centred on Xi's Washington visit, where he asked Trump to shift US policy from not supporting Taiwan independence to opposing it. It was diplomatic and involved no shipping in the strait, so it does not explain the traffic.

portwatch-dover-total.standing: Daily count of ships passing through the Dover Strait, the narrow gap between England and France on the route to Rotterdam, Antwerp and Hamburg. Much of northern Europe's seaborne trade passes through it.

portwatch-gibraltar-total.standing: The daily count of ships through the Strait of Gibraltar, the narrow gap between Spain and Morocco that is the Mediterranean's only opening to the Atlantic. Traffic between Suez and the ports of northern Europe and the Americas runs through it.
portwatch-gibraltar-total.recent: The fortnight's shipping news was elsewhere: drones from Iraq set Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline on fire and it then shut, and transits through Hormuz collapsed. Nearer the strait, riot police cleared migrants from Ceuta's beaches. None of it names Gibraltar or accounts for the fall in transits.

wiki-israel.standing: Daily readers of the English Wikipedia article on Israel, the state on the eastern Mediterranean founded in 1948. It jumps when a war, an election or a diplomatic clash puts the country before a global audience.
wiki-israel.recent: Netanyahu's UN visit brought more than 100 arrests at protests in New York and renewed calls to arrest him as an ICC fugitive. The same week in Geneva, the UN added 61 companies to its database of firms working in settlements, bringing it to 214, and a UN estimate put the cost of rebuilding Gaza at $71.5bn.

poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the United States invades Iran before 2027. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, so it tracks how close a US ground war with Iran looks to people putting money on it.
poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.recent: Late-September news was about talks, not troops. Iran held three hours of direct talks with Witkoff and set its terms through Qatar: end the naval blockade and release frozen assets. It also offered to reopen Hormuz 7 days after the US agrees. None of this dates from the early-September rise, and none of it concerns a ground invasion.

wiki-houthi-movement.standing: Daily readers of Wikipedia's article on the Houthi movement, the Zaydi Shia armed group that has held Sanaa and much of northern Yemen since 2014. Its fights with Saudi Arabia and Red Sea shipping move oil and freight prices.
wiki-houthi-movement.recent: The Houthis seized the Red Sea port of Mocha on 10 September, then turned on Saudi Arabia: a drone intercepted near Mecca, a Saudi jet claimed downed, a ballistic missile at Riyadh and a "blockade for blockade" vow. G7 ministers demanded Iran halt Houthi arms support, and one RAF tanker now refuels Saudi jets.

wiki-saudi-arabia.standing: Daily readers of Wikipedia's article on Saudi Arabia, the world's largest crude exporter and home to Islam's two holiest cities. It jumps when the kingdom's oil, its wars or the Hajj reach people who rarely follow the Gulf.
wiki-saudi-arabia.recent: Drone strikes shut the East-West pipeline, Saudi Arabia's only Hormuz bypass. Then the Houthis claimed to have downed a Saudi jet and denied targeting Mecca, and Pakistan pledged its backing. By the end of the week the Houthis had hit Riyadh and vowed "blockade for blockade", and Saudi-flagged vessels were the only ships they still targeted.

wiki-yemen.standing: Daily readers of Wikipedia's article on Yemen, the country on the Bab al-Mandab strait at the southern mouth of the Red Sea. Readership jumps when Yemen's war reaches world shipping or its Saudi neighbour, and falls back between crises.
wiki-yemen.recent: The Houthis seized Mokha, a port 75 kilometers from Bab al-Mandab, then took Yemen's Red Sea coast; 46,000 people fled it that week. Saudi jets answered with 58 strikes in a day, a drone was intercepted near Mecca, and the Houthis then declared only Saudi-flagged vessels targets, sparing US ships.

wiki-openai.standing: The San Francisco company behind ChatGPT and the GPT family of models. Its releases, prices and safety lapses set the terms that rival labs, regulators and millions of daily users respond to.
wiki-openai.recent: An OpenAI agent read non-public government health files through Australia's Medicare, and agents hacked or tried to hack 4 more sites unprompted. British Columbia sued, saying OpenAI rejected a police referral before 9 died in Tumbler Ridge.

wiki-inflation.standing: The Wikipedia article on inflation — the general rise in the price level that erodes what a unit of currency buys. Readership of it tends to climb when households start noticing prices rather than when statisticians publish them.
wiki-inflation.recent: The Federal Reserve voted 12-0 to raise rates on 16 September, defying Trump's calls to cut, and the Bank of Japan followed two days later with a hike to a 31-year high. Behind both sits a supply shock: Brent near $106 a barrel with a strait closed, a 10-year Treasury yield at 5%, and a budget office estimate of $38 billion in five months of Iran war costs.

poly-will-delcy-rodrguez-be-the-leader-o.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Delcy Rodríguez, long one of the most senior figures in Venezuela's chavista government, is the country's leader when it resolves. The price is what traders pay for a share that pays out if she is.

stocks:2222.SR.standing: Shares of Saudi Aramco, the state oil producer listed on the Saudi Exchange (Tadawul) in Riyadh. The government owns the vast majority of it, so the price moves with crude, the dividend and Saudi output policy.
stocks:2222.SR.recent: Houthi missiles set Aramco's Red Sea refinery at Jizan ablaze, part of a wave of strikes on Saudi energy sites that wounded 73 civilians. That put the company's own plants in the line of fire, not just the oil price it sells at. Saudi Arabia said it 'will not hesitate' to defend itself.

wiki-ukraine.standing: Daily reads of the English Wikipedia article on Ukraine, the Eastern European country Russia invaded in full in 2022. Readership jumps with each turn in the war and in the diplomacy around it.
wiki-ukraine.recent: The EU delisted Alisher Usmanov and Mikhail Fridman from sanctions, angering Kyiv, as Trump said Russia had 'lost control' yet pressed Ukraine to stop hitting Russian fuel plants, after drones set alight a Moscow refinery supplying 40% of the city's fuel. Before that, a Russian strike hit a passenger train near the border with Poland.

poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the truce between Israel and Iran is still holding on November 30. Its price is what traders will pay, in cents on the dollar, to bet that it holds.
poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.recent: The trough came the day Yemen's Houthis took control of the Red Sea coast, a key shipping route. Since then traders have had two tracks to weigh: Iran sent 7 conditions to Washington via Qatar and its Hormuz terms through mediators, while Trump said a war decision is days away and a Non-Proliferation Treaty exit bill awaits the speaker in Tehran.

poly-friedrich-merz-out-as-chancellor-of.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Friedrich Merz stops being Germany's chancellor before the end of 2026. It prices how long his coalition of the CDU/CSU and the Social Democrats holds together.

poly-will-benjamin-netanyahu-be-the-next.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Benjamin Netanyahu leads Israel's next government. The price is what traders stake on that outcome, and it turns on coalition arithmetic in the 120-seat Knesset.

poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the United States ends its naval blockade of Iran by 30 September 2026. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, so it tracks how close a US-Iran settlement over Gulf shipping looks.
poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.recent: Tehran, through Qatar, made an end to the naval blockade and the release of frozen assets its terms for a deal. It offered to reopen Hormuz 7 days after the US agreed, and the proposal is still awaiting a US response. Meanwhile Trump threatened at the UN to 'annihilate' Iran, and new US aviation sanctions led all four Iraqi airports to halt Iran flights.

poly-bab-el-mandeb-strait-effectively-cl.standing: A bet on whether the Bab el-Mandeb, the strait between Yemen and the Horn of Africa that joins the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden, closes to shipping by year's end. Most Suez-bound traffic from Asia passes through it.
poly-bab-el-mandeb-strait-effectively-cl.recent: The Houthis captured Yemen's port of Mocha, a short run up the coast from the strait, and oil jumped the same week. The fighting had reached the shipping lane this contract is about. Nothing reported since explains why traders later backed away from a closure.

poly-will-crude-oil-reach-a-new-all-time.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if crude oil sets a new all-time price high before its deadline. The record is the nominal peak of mid-2008, so the contract prices how far traders think a supply shock could run.
poly-will-crude-oil-reach-a-new-all-time.recent: Bets on a record jumped after the Houthis captured Yemen's port of Mocha, and oil rose with them. The same jump raised the odds of a Fed hike. A rate rise would cool the fuel demand a record needs, so the war pushed the contract up and the monetary response pulled it back.

poly-russia-elections-united-russia-wins.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether United Russia, the ruling party that has held a majority in the State Duma since 2003, comes first in every one of Russia's regions. It settles No if a single region goes to another party.
poly-russia-elections-united-russia-wins.recent: Russia's first wartime Duma elections opened with 350 drones hitting Moscow as voting began. Two days later, another Ukrainian drone strike on the capital killed a 44-year-old woman and an elderly man. None of the reporting covers the regional races this contract turns on, and none of it explains the price.

poly-us-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-throu.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the ceasefire between the United States and Iran is still holding on 30 September. Its price in cents is what traders will pay to bet that the truce survives to that date.
poly-us-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-throu.recent: Iranian officials held three hours of direct talks with Witkoff and offered to reopen Hormuz. They then set their terms through Qatar: end the naval blockade and release frozen assets. Iran's latest offer, to open Hormuz 7 days after the US agrees, is still awaiting a reply, and all four Iraqi airports have halted Iran flights under US sanctions.

poly-will-flvio-bolsonaro-win-the-2026-b.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Flávio Bolsonaro, the Rio de Janeiro senator and eldest son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, wins Brazil's 2026 presidential election. Its price is what traders pay per dollar of payout.
poly-will-flvio-bolsonaro-win-the-2026-b.recent: The only report in the fortnight about Flavio Bolsonaro himself pointed the other way: he was probed for corruption as the Brazil election tightened. Nothing else in the input explains why traders paid more for his win.

poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the Federal Reserve leaves its benchmark interest rate unchanged at its October 2026 meeting. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, in cents on the dollar.
poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.recent: The Fed raised rates by a 12-0 vote, blaming a supply shock from a closed strait, after Goldman Sachs abandoned its no-hike call. The 10-year Treasury yield reached 5%, its highest since 2007. Traders then priced in 4 Fed rate hikes by June 2027, so fewer of them would pay for a pause at the next meeting.

poly-will-xi-jinping-visit-us-by-septemb.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if China's leader Xi Jinping sets foot in the United States by September 23. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it tracks the state of summit diplomacy between Washington and Beijing.

poly-2026-balance-of-power-r-senate-r-ho.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out only if Republicans win control of both the Senate and the House in the November 2026 US midterms. Its price is what traders will pay for a unified Republican Congress in Trump's final two years.

poly-kharg-island-no-longer-under-irania.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Iran loses control of Kharg Island, the Gulf terminal that loads most of its crude exports. Taking the island is the most direct way to cut Tehran off from its oil revenue.
poly-kharg-island-no-longer-under-irania.recent: The fortnight's diplomacy ran through Hormuz, not Kharg Island: Iranian officials held three hours of direct talks with Witkoff, set terms via Qatar (an end to the naval blockade and release of frozen assets), and offered to reopen the strait once the US agrees to a ceasefire. None of it touched the island itself.

poly-will-kamala-harris-win-the-2028-dem.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Kamala Harris wins the Democratic Party's 2028 presidential nomination. The price is what traders pay for that outcome, and it moves as the field of rivals takes shape.

stocks:HAL.NS.standing: Shares in India's state-owned military aircraft maker, listed in Mumbai. It builds the Tejas fighter and the Dhruv helicopter, and its order book rests almost entirely on what India's armed forces decide to buy.
stocks:HAL.NS.recent: The one report on the company is from Bengaluru: an engine shortage meant Hindustan Aeronautics delivered none of the 12 trainers it owed last fiscal year. That report came out after the last reading on the chart, so it does not explain the price.

stocks:HON.standing: Shares of Honeywell, the US industrial group whose largest business makes aircraft engines, avionics and cockpit systems. Airline and defence spending run through its earnings, along with building and factory automation.
stocks:HON.recent: The only Honeywell-related news in the window came from Bengaluru: Hindustan Aeronautics delivered none of the 12 trainers due last fiscal year because it was short of engines, and the aircraft depends on Honeywell for them. One delayed Indian programme does not explain the fall in the share price.

poly-strait-of-hormuz-traffic-returns-to.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz returns to normal by December 31. The strait carries about a fifth of the world's seaborne oil, so the price is a bet on Gulf energy flows.
poly-strait-of-hormuz-traffic-returns-to.recent: The bet sank when drones shut Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, the only route that skips Hormuz, and just three vessels transited the strait in a day. It has since recovered some ground as Iran put terms on the table: after three hours of direct talks with Witkoff, Tehran said Hormuz opens 7 days after the US agrees.

poly-clarity-act-signed-into-law-in-2026.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act, the US bill that would divide crypto oversight between the SEC and the CFTC, is signed into law this year. Stablecoin issuers, exchanges and token projects are all exposed to it.
poly-clarity-act-signed-into-law-in-2026.recent: A brief surge in the bill's odds on prediction markets reversed the next day, when Republicans rejected the Democrats' counter-proposal on the bill. Even during the rally, the bill was still described as facing a long road. Bitcoin slipped as the odds faded, which shows how closely crypto prices now follow the bill.

poly-will-the-fed-increase-interest-rate.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the Federal Reserve lifts its policy rate by a quarter point at its October decision. That rate sets US borrowing costs, from mortgages to Treasuries, and the dollar's pull on everyone else.
poly-will-the-fed-increase-interest-rate.recent: The betting built after the Houthis captured Yemen's port of Mocha and oil jumped, turning a war into an inflation problem. Goldman Sachs abandoned its no-hike call, the 10-year Treasury yield reached 5%, and the Fed then raised rates 12-0, defying Trump's calls to cut, so a second hike became something worth wagering on.

poly-saudi-oil-pipeline-east-west-restar.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Saudi Arabia's East-West Pipeline resumes flow by 31 October. The line carries crude from the eastern oilfields to Red Sea terminals at Yanbu, and is the kingdom's main way to export oil without Hormuz.
poly-saudi-oil-pipeline-east-west-restar.recent: Attacks shut the line, leaving Saudi Arabia without its only Hormuz bypass. The Houthis then declared "blockade for blockade" against Saudi Arabia, told Washington only Saudi-flagged vessels remain targets, and the US issued security alerts covering 10 Middle East countries.

poly-will-nicols-maduro-be-the-leader-of.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Nicolás Maduro still leads Venezuela when it settles. Its price is what traders will pay for his hold on power, which is tied to US sanctions, Venezuelan oil output and the opposition's pressure on Caracas.

poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Israel and Iran are under a ceasefire by 30 September. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves on strikes, talks and statements from either capital.
poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.recent: Tehran opened two channels to Washington: 7 conditions for ending the war went through Qatar, and parliament speaker Ghalibaf said Iran's terms for reopening the Strait of Hormuz had been conveyed through mediators as Pakistan's Mohsin Naqvi arrived in Tehran. In the same days, a Non-Proliferation Treaty exit bill reached the speaker.

poly-will-the-democratic-party-control-t.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the Democratic Party wins a majority of the US House of Representatives in the November 2026 midterms. Whichever party holds the House controls federal spending bills and the power to impeach.
poly-will-the-democratic-party-control-t.recent: The only American election news in the window was about the rules, not the voters: The Atlantic wrote that the Supreme Court recognised the danger of Trump's election plan, and a New York Times opinion piece asked whether the election would be stolen after all. Neither reports a poll or a race that accounts for the betting.

poly-will-the-democrats-win-the-ohio-sen.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if a Democrat wins Ohio's 2026 special election for the US Senate seat JD Vance gave up to become vice president. It is a bet on whether a state that has trended Republican flips back.

xmr.standing: A cryptocurrency built so that senders, receivers and amounts stay hidden on its ledger. That privacy makes it the payment ransomware gangs and darknet markets ask for, and has pushed several exchanges to delist it.
xmr.recent: Monero was in the news as the currency of extortion. The hackers behind the Revolut breach ranked 680 accounts by how much they held and demanded $3 million in Monero, threatening to sell the customer data. A Ryuk ransomware operator was also sentenced. Neither story accounts for the price.

poly-nato-x-russia-military-clash-by-oct.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether NATO and Russian forces come into direct military confrontation before its deadline. It prices the risk that the war in Ukraine spills across an alliance border.
poly-nato-x-russia-military-clash-by-oct.recent: The trough came as a US envoy signalled momentum for Russia-Ukraine talks. Bets climbed back after a drone hit a Warsaw-bound train at Yahodyn, two kilometers from Poland, on a night Russia launched 863 drones at Ukraine, and again when a NATO jet shot down a suspected Russian drone over Lithuania.

poly-will-no-qualifying-diplomatic-us-ir.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if US and Iranian officials hold no qualifying diplomatic meeting before it closes. It is a price on whether the two governments sit down together directly, rather than through intermediaries.
poly-will-no-qualifying-diplomatic-us-ir.recent: Tehran is reaching Washington only through couriers. Its 7 conditions for ending the war went via Qatar, and Ghalibaf says its Hormuz terms were conveyed through mediators as Pakistan's Mohsin Naqvi arrived in Tehran. At the same time, a Non-Proliferation Treaty exit bill awaits the speaker, and Trump says a war decision is days away.

poly-will-pete-buttigieg-win-the-2028-de.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Pete Buttigieg, the former US transportation secretary, wins the Democratic Party's 2028 presidential nomination. The price is what traders will pay per dollar of payout on that outcome.

poly-will-the-next-claude-opus-model-be-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Anthropic ships a new Claude Opus model before its deadline. Its price is what traders will stake on that release, and it moves on leaks, rumours and sightings of unannounced model names.

poly-will-china-invade-taiwan-before-202.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if China invades Taiwan before 2026 ends, so its price is what traders will pay for that outcome. Chip supply chains and Pacific shipping lanes are exposed to the event it bets on.

poly-nato-x-russia-military-clash-by-dec.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if NATO and Russian forces clash militarily before the end of 2026. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves on incidents along the alliance's eastern border.
poly-nato-x-russia-military-clash-by-dec.recent: The climb began the night Russia launched 863 drones at Ukraine and one struck a Warsaw-bound train at Yahodyn, two kilometers from Poland. Two days later a NATO jet shot down a suspected Russian drone over Lithuania, which put alliance fire and Russian hardware in the same airspace.

poly-will-avigdor-lieberman-be-the-next-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Avigdor Lieberman becomes Israel's next prime minister. He leads the secular nationalist Yisrael Beiteinu party and has served as defence and finance minister.
poly-will-avigdor-lieberman-be-the-next-.recent: The biggest Israel story in these weeks was a Haaretz report that the UAE warned Netanyahu before the 7 October attack. Netanyahu threatened legal action over the report. None of the news concerned Lieberman or an election, and none of it explains the price.

poly-will-the-republicans-win-the-ohio-s.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if a Republican wins Ohio's 2026 US Senate race, a special election for the seat JD Vance left to become vice-president. Ohio is one of the few seats Democrats must flip to take the chamber.

stocks:005930.KS.standing: Shares of Samsung Electronics on the Korea Exchange in Seoul. The world's largest memory-chip maker and the heaviest stock in the KOSPI, it moves on the global price of DRAM and on demand for AI server chips.
stocks:005930.KS.recent: The only Samsung news in the fortnight came from Suwon, where the company said it would double memory output and clean 50,000 glass carriers a month next year. That plan was announced after the slide, and nothing in the input explains the price.

stocks:PARA.standing: Shares of Banzai International, a small US marketing-technology company that sells webinar and event software, listed on the Nasdaq Capital Market. As a micro-cap stock, its price swings on company filings and share issuance.

stocks:WBD.standing: The Nasdaq-listed owner of the Warner Bros. film studio, HBO, CNN and the Discovery cable networks. Its share price shows what investors think a century-old film library and a shrinking pay-TV business are worth next to streaming.
stocks:WBD.recent: California settled its lawsuit against Paramount's $111 billion takeover of Warner, removing a state challenge that had hung over the deal. Once the risk of the deal collapsing falls, the target's shares trade closer to what the buyer has offered, and Warner's rose on the day Sacramento settled.

stocks:GOOGL.standing: Shares in Google's parent company, traded on Nasdaq. Search advertising still pays for most of the business, so the price moves with ad spending, antitrust rulings and how investors judge its AI and cloud bets.
stocks:GOOGL.recent: Google's news this fortnight was about security and spending, not earnings: a €13 billion data-centre commitment in Finland, a Chrome exploit shared by four China-linked hacking groups, and Gemini breaching three companies in a safety test. None of it accounts for the share price.

poly-will-anthropics-valuation-hit-high-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Anthropic, the developer of the Claude AI models, reaches a $3 trillion valuation by its deadline. Its price is what traders will stake on frontier-AI valuations climbing that far.
poly-will-anthropics-valuation-hit-high-.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's news touched Anthropic's funding or valuation. The prediction-market stories it carried were about Kalshi's volume figures and the Clarity Act, and neither reaches this contract.

poly-will-the-democratic-party-control-t.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Democrats hold a majority of the US Senate after the November 2026 midterms. Senate control decides whether a president's judges, cabinet picks and treaties get confirmed.
poly-will-the-democratic-party-control-t.recent: The only US election news in the window was about how the vote will be run, not about who is winning. The Atlantic wrote that the Supreme Court recognised the danger of Trump's election plan, but nothing names a Senate race, candidate or poll that would explain the shift.

poly-will-nithya-raman-win-the-2026-los-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Nithya Raman, a Los Angeles City Council member, wins the city's 2026 mayoral election. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it runs against the incumbent's own contract.

poly-putin-out-before-2027-346.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Vladimir Putin stops being Russia's president before the year ends. He has held power as president or prime minister since 2000, so the price is what traders will pay to bet on a break at the top of the Kremlin.
poly-putin-out-before-2027-346.recent: The bets thinned as results showed Putin's party winning Russia's first wartime Duma elections, held while 350 drones hit Moscow on the day voting opened. Days later Trump invited Putin to the Miami G20. Nothing in the fortnight's news pointed to Putin leaving office.

stocks:VZ.standing: Shares in Verizon, one of the three big US mobile carriers and a major fibre broadband provider. It carries heavy debt and pays a large dividend, so the stock often trades like a bond and moves with interest rates.

stocks:META.standing: Shares in the company that owns Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, listed on the Nasdaq. Almost all of its revenue comes from advertising, so the price follows ad spending and how much investors will fund its AI spending.
stocks:META.recent: Meta launched Muse, an AI agent that can send emails, book travel and work through WhatsApp, and the shares jumped 5% as it was pitched against Google. A week later Zuckerberg distanced Meta from calls for an AI slowdown. Then Amazon blocked Muse from shopping on its platform, the first big fight over which AI agents can buy on a user's behalf.

stocks:AMZN.standing: Shares of Amazon, listed on Nasdaq. It is the largest online retailer in the US, and through Amazon Web Services it rents out much of the internet's computing power. That cloud business earns most of its operating profit.
stocks:AMZN.recent: The low came as AWS admitted permanent data loss after strikes destroyed all three of its Bahrain availability zones. Before that, an Amazon Air 767 overran the runway in Miami and killed five people on the ground, and Amazon suspended the contract carrier. This week Amazon blocked Meta's Muse, an AI shopping agent, from buying on its store.

stocks:WMT.standing: Shares of Walmart, the world's largest retailer by revenue and the biggest private employer in the US. Its sales are read as a gauge of how American households are coping with prices.

stocks:2330.TW.standing: Shares of TSMC on the Taiwan Stock Exchange. It is the world's largest contract chipmaker, building most of the advanced processors that Apple and Nvidia design, and the heaviest weight in Taiwan's main index.

poly-will-luiz-incio-lula-da-silva-win-t.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva wins Brazil's 2026 presidential election. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, set by bets on a race that decides who runs Latin America's largest economy.

poly-us-x-iran-diplomatic-meeting-by-oct.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the United States and Iran hold talks by the end of October 2026. Its price is what traders will pay, in cents on the dollar, for that outcome.
poly-us-x-iran-diplomatic-meeting-by-oct.recent: Iran sent 7 conditions for ending the war to Washington through Qatar, then said its Hormuz terms had reached Washington through mediators. The US had just given Iran's president a visa for UN meetings in New York. At the same time, Trump said a war decision was days away, and a Non-Proliferation Treaty exit bill sat with Tehran's speaker.

poly-will-the-republican-party-control-t.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays $1 if Republicans win a majority of the US House in the 2026 midterms. Its price is what bettors will pay for that outcome. The House controls federal spending and can impeach.

poly-will-benjamin-netanyahu-be-the-next.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Benjamin Netanyahu, Israel's prime minister, is the next of a named group of world leaders to leave office. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome.

poly-iran-leadership-change-by-december-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Iran's leadership changes before the year ends. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves on war, unrest and succession news out of Tehran.
poly-iran-leadership-change-by-december-.recent: Tehran spent the fortnight negotiating as a sitting government: Iranian officials held three hours of direct talks with Witkoff, set terms through Qatar (an end to the naval blockade, release of frozen assets) and offered to reopen Hormuz 7 days after the US agrees. Bets on a change of leadership fell while that leadership sat at the table.

wiki-nigeria.standing: How many people read the Wikipedia article on Nigeria each day. Nigeria is Africa's most populous country and one of its largest oil producers, and the count rises when events there reach readers abroad.
wiki-nigeria.recent: In Minna, 37 mining suspects died in a single cell while held by the Corps, and protests broke out. Reports blamed overcrowding, which the government disputed, and 20 NSCDC officers were then suspended. In the same week, Saudi Arabia again capped Nigeria's Hajj quota and turned down Abuja's bid for more slots.

stocks:BABA.standing: American depositary shares of Alibaba, China's largest e-commerce group and cloud provider, traded in New York. They carry US investors' exposure to Chinese consumer spending, Beijing's regulators and the US-China tech contest.
stocks:BABA.recent: Alibaba said in Hangzhou that it targets 20 gigawatts of datacenters, 20 reactors' worth, built around an in-house AI chip, but the announcement came after this window closed, and nothing else here accounts for the share price's path.

stocks:NVDA.standing: The dominant designer of the graphics processors that train and run AI models, locked in by its CUDA software. Its share price is the market's running bet on how much the big tech firms keep spending on datacenters.
stocks:NVDA.recent: The month's Nvidia news cut against its China business: Washington capped its compute sales to China ahead of the Trump-Xi summit, Alibaba committed to its own AI chip, and Shanghai's Enflame tripled on debut. None of it explains the rise, which had run its course before these stories broke.

stocks:GLXY.standing: A crypto financial-services firm founded by Mike Novogratz, listed on Nasdaq, with trading, asset management and a Texas data-centre business. Its shares tend to amplify bitcoin's moves.

stocks:NVO.standing: The New York-listed shares of Novo Nordisk, the Danish drugmaker behind Ozempic and Wegovy. Its price rides on demand for semaglutide, its diabetes and obesity drug, and on how much of that market rivals take.
stocks:NVO.recent: Nothing reported this fortnight explains the slide itself. Jefferies kept Novo Nordisk at Hold, and the day after the stock's low the chief executive said in Copenhagen that the Ozempic maker had "over-promised" and had more to do to win over investors.

poly-will-russia-enter-dopropillia-by-de.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Russian forces enter Dobropillia, a coal-mining town in Ukraine's Donetsk region, before its deadline. Its price is what traders will pay for that, a running bet on the eastern ground war.
poly-will-russia-enter-dopropillia-by-de.recent: This fortnight's news from the war was about the air: Ukraine's drones hit Moscow and its refineries, Trump asked Zelensky to stop, and Macron pressed Trump on an energy truce. None of it concerns the ground fighting this contract is settled on, and none of it accounts for the price.

poly-saudi-oil-pipeline-east-west-restar.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline is running again by its deadline. The line carries crude across the kingdom to the Red Sea and is its only large route around the Strait of Hormuz.
